subject: SparkCart embed: proposed stabilization steps, product exceptions, and customer commit
messages:
From: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: tim@sparkcart.com
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SparkCart embed: latency spike — quick stabilization proposal + customer note

Team — observed an intermittent p95/p99 lift on the SparkCart checkout embed between 08:30–08:55 PT this morning. Telemetry shows a sharp fanout of small requests (avg seq len ~12) that correlates with an increase in KV misses and a transient increase in kernel time on a subset of host pools. Customer is seeing ~3–4s response times on some requests (their SLA is 1.5s).

Immediate asks:
- Karthik / SRE: can you confirm whether this is KV cache evaporation vs. scheduler batching mismatch? Quick triage logs attached (snapshot-heap-log.txt). If KV warmup helps, can we run a targeted warmup to the SparkCart route for the next 30m and hold?
- Ben / Runtime: is there a safe, short-lived routing override we can toggle (route to the lower-latency small-seq variant) without a full rollout? We need something that avoids degraded quality.
- Marissa / Product: do we have permission to enable a quantized variant (int8) as a temporary fallback for this customer? I know we usually require customer sign-off for model changes; given outage risk I want to propose a temporary exception with a rollback window.

Customer communication: I drafted a short note below (to Tim) — if you approve I will send. Tim is CC'd for visibility.

P.S. If we need executive sign-off for the exception, call it out and I'll escalate.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: tim@sparkcart.com
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SparkCart embed: latency spike — quick stabilization proposal + customer note

On Sun, May 17, 2026 at 09:12, priya.natarajan@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — observed an intermittent p95/p99 lift...

Quick triage notes:
- KV cache: eviction spikes on the host pool serving SparkCart look plausible — we see a correlated GC/heap growth on two hosts. Attachment shows heap snapshot at peak.
- Batching: the small-seq fanout is causing less efficient kernel utilization; runtime is spending more time per token in the hot path.

Immediate mitigations I can do in next 15–30m:
1) Issue a targeted warmup for sparkcart-route on the affected pool (30 minutes) — will prepopulate KV and should reduce tail.
2) Temporarily increase the min-batch-window for that route from 1ms to 5ms to increase batch efficiency; this will slightly increase median but reduce tail.
3) Add a routing override to shed to the small-sequence optimized pool (if Ben gives the toggle).

Risks: warmup+batch-window is low risk. Routing override to quantized variant requires product/CS sign-off because it may change token-level outputs. If we have customer approval we can do an opt-in toggle and monitor.

I'll run the warmup now and report back in 20 minutes.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: snapshot-heap-log.txt (see heap growth annotations)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SparkCart embed: latency spike — quick stabilization proposal + customer note

Thanks for the quick triage. Product stance:
- Temporary routing to a lower-latency optimized pool (same model) or batch-window changes are fine — no product approval required for config-level fallbacks. Please include the rollback plan and monitoring thresholds.
- Quantized model (int8) is considered a model variant. We need one of the following before enabling for a customer: (a) explicit customer consent, or (b) SRE/Product agreement to a timeboxed exception with a pre-approved rollback. Given the severity, I can approve a 4-hour exception if CS and legal are looped and we offer the customer an SLA credit if quality changes are observed.

If you want to enable quantization as a fallback, I need:
- A test prompt set (we can reuse the SparkCart QA checklist)
- A monitoring threshold for diff-rate (e.g., >2% token-diff or >1% output-delta triggers rollback)

Attaching the QA checklist for quick review.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Product — Inference Platform

Attachment: product-qa-checklist.pdf
From: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: tim@sparkcart.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: SparkCart embed: brief update and proposed immediate stabilization (draft)

Tim — quick update and an ask for permission. We're investigating a transient tail-latency increase on the SparkCart checkout embed and have a short stabilization plan that should reduce the highest tail latencies within 30–60 minutes. Proposed immediate actions (we'd like your approval to proceed):

1) Targeted warmup of your route on the affected host pool (this prepopulates internal caches) — low risk.
2) Temporary increase to the batching min-window for your route to improve GPU kernel efficiency — slight median increase expected but should reduce the 99th percentile.
3) Optional: timeboxed fallback to an int8 quantized variant for up to 4 hours (if you approve). We expect small changes in tokenization/wording at the ~<1–2% level for the highest-risk prompts; we would monitor a short prompt set and immediately roll back if we exceed the agreed thresholds. If you prefer we will not enable the quantized fallback until after you approve.

We'll send a short post-incident summary once the tail is back to normal. If you approve the warmup and batching change, I will initiate them immediately. If you want the quantized fallback we need a quick go/no-go.

Draft customer note attached (cust-message-draft.txt).

Thanks — Priya

From: tim@sparkcart.com
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SparkCart embed: brief update and proposed immediate stabilization (draft)

Thanks Priya — please proceed with actions 1 and 2 immediately. Do NOT enable the quantized fallback without explicit confirmation from our side; we prefer the kernel/batching fixes first. Appreciate the SLA credit offer if there is measurable user impact. Keep us posted — Tim
